$comment: Assets owned by gems that expect a Rails asset pipeline, mapped into our esbuild build.
Shared by esbuild.config.js and test/assets/asset_mappings_test.rb; `bundle info <gem> --path`
is the only runtime link between them. Paths are relative to the gem root.
assetPaths mirrors `config.assets.paths`: where a gem's assets are found, and what the audit
test asserts. manifestEntries is what Ruby names and so needs a manifest key. The two do not
line up — assets referenced from a gem's own CSS or JS arrive through assetPaths alone.
auditOnly marks a path the gem registers but our build never resolves through. esbuild skips
those, so the flag is load-bearing: mark a path that is actually needed and the build fails.
logicalName is the helper argument minus its extension; `*` becomes the file's basename.
The audit sees only explicit registrations; Propshaft also adds each engine's app/assets/*
implicitly. We ship our own avo-overrides rather than rely on that.

assetPaths.$comment: Prebuilt CSS and JS, under the logical names Avo's layout asks for.
Logos and favicons. Also resolves the webfonts: avo/application.css asks for url(fonts/…), meaning logical avo/fonts/…
These icons get inlined by avo-icons from disk.
Sprockets-style path for a bare "fonts/…" lookup. We reach the fonts via app/assets/images instead.

manifestEntries.$comment: e.g. image_tag("avo/logo.png"). Glob is not recursive, so webfonts one directory down are excluded. The stylesheet already pulls them in.
